# Attention, mentions, and messages

English | [中文](attention-and-messaging.zh.md)

## Thread Attention and Inbox
Attention is durable private state for one Member and Thread: current period start and contiguous read watermark. Creating a Thread (its author follows), creating a Task Claim, or explicitly following starts it. Taskless Threads can be unfollowed directly; taskful Threads require no active Claim. Unfollow ends the period and discards its unread work; a later follow starts at the current tail.

While active, other Members' Messages—and taskful Claim and Task resolution Activities—become ordinary unread. Mentions create durable direct markers. The sender's own mutation is not unread. Promotion creates a `promote` Activity for current followers. Follow/unfollow/read are private and do not advance Thread revision.

The first read returns the anchor, optional Task/Claim snapshot, limited recent background, and bounded unread batch. Background is orientation and already read. `history` is the only older-facts pager, and a Member re-entering a Thread it has read before receives no background — its orientation there is the anchor and the batch alone, so the facts between are its own to page back to.

Human navigation is Workspace → Project → Thread; a Task is an overlay, not a navigation level. The Inbox is a global Team page that opens from the sidebar card/narrow-rail icon and merges every visible Workspace's Inbox calls — the reader's whole unread slice, mentions counted inside it rather than alone. Opening it performs no Thread read, and only opening a Thread advances the watermark and clears its direct and private reminder markers. A private Task reminder is a direct notification, not a mention or a public Activity; reading the Inbox or board never consumes it.

Opening a Thread performs durable Human read and scrolls to the latest fact; a bounded result with remaining unread drains automatically through continued reads, so no explicit continuation exists. History does not acknowledge new work. Arrivals while the Thread is open are acknowledged durably regardless of scroll position; a reader away from the bottom sees only a pure jump hint with no read semantics.

An Inbox call answers a bounded queue: at most `limit` unread Threads (1–100, default 50), with `hasMore` stating whether Threads remain beyond that page, and the Client prints that verdict where its list ends. Reading a Thread drains it from the queue, so the rows a full page hid become reachable without a cursor — which the projection deliberately does not carry.

## Mentions
A Message names its recipients in its own body: writing `@Handle` is what makes a mention, matched against the Project's addressable names case-insensitively, on Unicode word boundaries, and longest handle first, so a name the Client renders as a chip is the same name that delivers. A bare handle stays ordinary prose, and a handle inside a code block or code span is quoted rather than called. `@all` is plain text under rules version 2: it notifies no one, so every Member that must be reached is named.

No recipient parameter exists: the Host resolves the body for a Human composing in the Web Client and for an Agent composing through `team_message` alike. The Human is addressable the same way, as `@human` — a permanent alias that survives renames (the current display name from `team_view` addresses them too, and chips render that name either way). No agent handle may claim the `human` literal, so the alias never notifies anyone else.

A mention — in a Thread start, a reply, or a Main stream post — delivers its Message to the named Member once and never starts or resumes Attention: following is a Member's own explicit choice. Every addressable Member of the Project can be mentioned; there is no invitation step.

Agents may mention the Human without making the Human a follower.

A reply answers one existing Message, so it also carries that Message's author as a recipient: quoting a Member delivers to them exactly as naming them does.

The author joins the recipient set before delivery is resolved, under the same direct-marker rule, and the Human is never a recipient because they read the Thread directly. A Message's own author is never added to itself, so answering your own Message notifies nobody.

A reply whose target is unknown, or belongs to another Thread, is refused rather than recorded.

A direct-mention notice names the Message it carries and, when that Message answers another, the one it answers: `Message ref` is the Message being delivered, and `Replies to` is its parent. Without that line a recipient knows it was answered but not what it said, and the answer it sends back is a guess.

The line states the parent's author and the first line of its body, with the full ref last: `Replies to: @handle — "first line" [message:<uuid>]`. The ref is what the reader hands back — to `team_message.replyToMessageRef` to answer it, or to `team_thread message` to read the body whole. A parent that no longer resolves, which an archived Project causes, leaves the line as the bare ref: the ref is still true and a summary would not be.

## Human-readable messages
Every message leads with the conclusion or state; mechanical detail — `file:line`, commands, hashes, probe output — follows below it, and detail a peer Member needs is never dropped, only moved. Prose stays in the language the Human writes, while identifiers, paths, commands, and refs stay verbatim.

Mentioning the Human — writing `@human` in the body — is how the Human is notified; the mention creates the durable direct marker the Human Inbox surfaces, and nothing else does. The minimum set that mentions the Human: a Human decision is owed; a Claim is finished and waits for acceptance; a blocker or risk the Human must know about; progress the Human explicitly asked for. Mid-thread progress chatter between Agents stays Agent-to-Agent and mentions no Human. The persona states this contract and the `team_message` body description restates its opening rule where the model composes the body.

A mention opens with the answer in one to three readable sentences; when a decision is owed, it says plainly what needs deciding and what happens by default if nobody answers — no fixed template. Message shape is a convention the Inbox ignores: it counts mentions, never formatting.

## Ref citation
Team tools return branded refs (`task:`, `thread:`, `project:`, `member:`, `claim:`) with full UUIDs; reuse them verbatim when quoting. A ref whose UUID is truncated still resolves when its first 6+ hex characters are unambiguous: `task:0f0ad7` addresses the Task whose UUID starts with `0f0ad7`. A prefix shared by several refs is rejected with the candidate full refs, and a prefix shorter than 6 hex characters is not accepted — lengthen the prefix or quote the full ref.

Abbreviated refs obey the same boundaries as full refs: Tasks and Threads under archived Projects stay unreachable, and the Client renders a ref as a link only when it resolves uniquely, leaving unresolvable text plain.

- 08 发布前的两次重放修复：legacy 读取快照按写入时代的 direct 规则校验（mention-only）；06/07 未发布 dev 形状（Task 创建无活动、Claim 转换无责任 marker）按当时写入的样子重放。真实开发账本因此无需重建，此前的「中间 v2 账本重建」口径由这两项容忍取代；10-25 曾误截掉 32 条真实使用（owner 指派与主对话消息），已从备份完整恢复，教训是截断真实账本前必须按 occurredAt 与用户核对数据归属。
- `spec.md` §13 三项探针：DM 的 Workspace 边界已在 Host `sendDm` 校验；旧 accept 缺 `acceptedClaimRefs` 时已有回退，03 补测试；规则标记与启动恢复的写入顺序已在 03 查清并由 `initialize()` 保证。
- 版本 2 的规则在 04–06 间逐步落地；预览开关 `DSH_AGENT_TEAM_PREVIEW_RULES` 已移除，版本 2 是默认规则，无需任何环境变量。
- 08 已完成：Task 带 `accountable` 与不可变 `sourceThreadRefs`（仅同 Project 无 Task 讨论）；Agent 仅可验收 `in_review` 且从未持有该 Task 任何 Claim（含 released），执行过的 accountable 只能 close/reopen/transfer；close/reopen/transfer 限 Human 或当前 accountable，已结束 Task 仅 Human 可转交；owner 撤销/离开/归档/删除在同一 operation 把 open Task 原子转回 Human 并记公开 transfer 活动（Project 归档对全部 owner 生效，suspend 保留）；责任事件按角色进 Inbox direct 级（activity marker 计入 direct，投递一律 immediate）；看板带 `relation: 'accountable'` 与 `needsAcceptance`；来源 Task 不进 Main stream，来源讨论以只读卡片投影显示（不改 revision、不产生未读）；`team_task` 增加 accept/close/reopen/transfer，`team_message.start` 支持 accountable 与来源；persona 与 skill 同步。遗留：suspend 的「负责人已暂停」界面提示、Agent 侧 `team_thread` 渲染来源讨论派生 Task 卡（Host 已返回 `taskCards`）归入 09。Human 项目看板与全局看板已显示负责人（你负责/负责人 X）与「待你验收」徽标（Host 条目带 `accountableOwner`）。
- 09 已完成：事件评估的待验收/停滞提醒（durable episode 跨重启去重、私有 marker 仅 Task Thread read 消费、无 timer、Agent idle 仅进程内可确认观测、写入边界防交错、生命周期清理补齐）；来源讨论 Agent Task 卡与「负责人已暂停」显示同批交付。最终验证 1279 单测通过、1 跳过，真实 Web 8/8，真实账本 24565 条全量重放通过。首次历史数据有 4 个 Human-time 候选，后续只在 Team 事件评估点写入，不主动定时补发。

## 完成条件

- [x] 01 读得懂 Project 写法的发布
- [x] 02 Channel 全仓改名为 Project（真实 ledger 验收待 Human）
- [x] 03 规则版本机制
- [x] 04 Agent owner 与 Project member 派生
- [x] 05 项目主对话与开 Thread 权限
- [x] 06 按责任投递、Inbox 与 Agent 指引；启用规则版本 2（交付后 Human 在 dev profile 试用一周，按 `spec.md` §11 的指标复盘再继续）
- [x] 07 Task board 投影与 `team_task`
- [x] 08 Task 负责人、转交与验收限制（属于最终规则版本 2；suspend 的界面提示归入 09）
- [x] 09 待验收积压与停滞提醒
- [ ] durable 结论进入正式文档双语对与 `CHANGELOG.md`
- [ ] 面向外部使用者的升级说明：升级后所有项目只有 Human owner，需重新指定 Agent owner；先备份 `agent_team.sqlite`；不承诺降级

## 正式文档出口

`docs/domain-model.zh.md`（Project、Project member、owner、accountable、Main stream）、`docs/team-collaboration/boundaries.zh.md`（权限与 fence）、`docs/team-collaboration/attention-and-messaging.zh.md`（Inbox、投递等级、mention 与回复）、`docs/team-collaboration/tools.zh.md`（七工具，含 `team_task`）、`docs/team-collaboration/model-and-time.zh.md`（事件评估的时间条件）、`docs/architecture/tools-and-preset.zh.md`（persona 与 core skill）、`docs/frontend-design/components.zh.md`（composer、卡片、看板）的双语对，以及 `CHANGELOG.md`。九张工单交付后，本目录移入 `.scratch/archive/<完成月份>/`，并按 `.scratch/AGENTS.md` 把该移动 amend 进交付它的 commit。

## 调研证据

- 真实 ledger 60 天使用审计（24293 条 operation）与 22 个未归档 Channel 的参与度统计，摘要见 `spec.md` §0、§14。统计脚本与原始报告在 `/tmp/team-audit/`、`/tmp/channel-participation/`（临时产物，未入库）。
- Raft 的 11 篇一手 blog：pull-based inbox、构造初始 context、builder ≠ verifier。

## 与其它工作项的关系

`channel-page-redesign` 的 issue 04（看板的数据源与归属）由本模型取代：看板改读 Host 的 Task board 投影（工单 03）。该工作项其余三张票已合入 master，作为本模型的 UI 前提保留。

Contents of /home/yu/projects/dsh-agent-team/.scratch/AGENTS.md:

# .scratch Work Rules

This subtree holds cross-session work items: design snapshots, research, implementation tickets, prototypes, and acceptance evidence. It is not an implementation or API authority — current behavior is defined by `packages/` source and tests, and maintenance rules by [`../docs/AGENTS.md`](../docs/AGENTS.md). This file only governs how to work here.

## Work-item structure

Each `active/<work>/` is one directory with a short `README.md` as its single continuation entry, covering five items: status, last-checked date, current frontier (who is doing what and what is blocked), completion conditions, and the formal-doc exit.

```
active/<work>/
├── README.md      # continuation entry (the five items above)
├── spec.md        # confirmed decision snapshot — written once discussion converges
├── issues/        # tracer-bullet implementation tickets, one file per ticket
│   ├── 01-<slug>.md
│   └── 02-<slug>.md
├── materials/     # research and external material (keep only what is worth re-reading)
└── validation/    # human-confirmed acceptance evidence (see the development doc)
```

## Ticket discipline

Each `issues/NN-<slug>.md` uses a fixed skeleton, numbered from `01` in dependency order (blockers first):

```markdown
# NN — title

**What to build:** the end-to-end behavior this ticket demonstrably delivers once done (user perspective, not a layered task list)
**Blocked by:** the tickets blocking it, or "None — can start immediately"
**Status:** pending | ready | in-progress | complete

- [ ] acceptance criterion 1
- [ ] acceptance criterion 2
```

- **Vertical slices**: each ticket cuts one narrow, complete path through every layer (schema → API → UI → tests), independently verifiable when done; no horizontal division of labor by layer.
- **Self-contained tickets**: each ticket can start in a new context without reading the whole work-item history. Avoid concrete file paths and code snippets (they go stale); exception: decision-dense fragments from prototypes (state machines, type shapes) may be inlined with their source noted.
- **Frontier workflow**: tickets whose blockers are all done form the frontier and are ready to start; a serial chain runs top to bottom. Tickets that are written but still carry unfinished blockers stay **pending**, so `ready` always means startable now.
- **Wide-refactor exception**: when one mechanical change's blast radius covers the whole repository, do not force it into a tracer bullet — order it as expand–contract: expand first (old and new coexist), migrate in batches, then contract (delete the old form).

## Lifecycle

- **Closing a work item**: close or delete unfinished tickets → move durable conclusions into the `../docs/` maintained documents → delete process material without provenance value → move into `archive/YYYY-MM/`.
- **Archive is history**: archived states and terminology only represent the working context of their time and never override current implementation; do not rewrite archives to match new code.
- **Transient artifacts**: logs, debug screenshots, and downloads go in `local/` or `artifacts/` (gitignored), never into active or archive.

## Version control

- **Active does not enter version history**: while a work item is open, its `active/<work>/` directory is gitignored working material. Force-add it (`git add -f`) only when a reviewer must see it.
- **Archive enters history on close**: when a work item closes, move it into `archive/YYYY-MM/` and amend that move into the commit(s) that deliver the work, so the archive records what actually shipped instead of sitting in a scratch-only commit at the tip.

## Directory index

See [README.md](README.md).

1	# Changelog
2	
3	All notable changes to this project are documented in this file. The format follows [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/) and Semantic Versioning. Team bundle versions evolve independently of DeepSeek Harness versions; DeepSeek Harness compatibility is expressed through `peerDependencies` and [`docs/dsh-release-compatibility.md`](docs/dsh-release-compatibility.md).
4	
5	## [Unreleased]
6	
7	**Upgrade note**
8	
9	- Rules version 2 is now the default and the `DSH_AGENT_TEAM_PREVIEW_RULES` preview switch is gone: this build adopts version 2 on every ledger it opens and no longer writes the version 1 kinds it replaced (`team/message-sent`; they replay inside version 1 segments only). A build at or below 0.2.5 refuses a ledger this build has opened, so install this release on every profile that shares `$DSH_HOME/storages/` before opening the Team anywhere, and back up `agent_team.sqlite` first. A ledger written by the unreleased 06/07 dev builds of this train still opens: their Task starts without a creation activity and their Claim transitions without responsibility markers replay exactly as those builds wrote them.
10	
11	**New**
12	
13	- Tasks carry one accountable owner. An Agent Project owner creating a Task becomes accountable by default; the Human may name any owner. Accountability transfers explicitly to another owner or the Human; when an owner is withdrawn, archived, removed, or leaves a Workspace, every open Task it was accountable for returns to the Human in the same operation with a public transfer activity.
14	- Acceptance is separated from execution: an Agent may accept a Task only once it is `in_review` and only if it never held any Claim on it, released ones included; the Human keeps early acceptance. Close, reopen, and transfer belong to the Human and the current accountable owner.
15	- Responsibility events reach the Inbox as direct facts regardless of Attention: being made accountable, entering review, a Task left unowned, reopen, and needs-your-acceptance when the accountable owner executed the work.
16	- A Task may record its originating discussion (`sourceThreadRefs`, immutable, same Project); sourced Tasks leave the Main stream and appear as read-only cards inside the discussions they came from. The board adds the `accountable` relation and flags Tasks awaiting an owner's acceptance.
17	- `team_task` gains `accept`, `close`, `reopen`, and `transfer`; `team_message.start` accepts an accountable owner and source discussions for Tasks. The persona and the `team-domain-model` skill state the accountable/verifier split.
18	- Notices are delivered by role. A Project owner's Main stream posts, new discussions, mentions, replies, and ownership events wake immediately; an owner's or Task owner's ordinary Thread updates accumulate per Member per Thread and summarize once at five. The sender's own messages never enter the sender's Inbox.
19	- Every visible Project carries one Main stream unread row in the Inbox, shared by the Human and Agents; `team_inbox` and the Human's inbox count agree.
20	- The task board: a `taskBoard` Host projection and Remote method lists every visible Project's open Tasks plus the last five finished per Project, and names the reader its `humanMemberId`. The Web Client reads this projection in both places — the Project board tab and the cross-Workspace Task board page the sidebar's 任务看板 entry opens (its own checklist glyph, a narrow-rail button, cards that say 「你负责」, and an empty state that stands alone without column heads). `team_claim` is merged into `team_task` (`board`, `list`, `claim`, `done`, `release`, `promote`); `team_view` no longer returns active task threads.
21	- The team-member persona is rewritten for project ownership and ships the `team-domain-model` core skill.
22	- Event-evaluated Task reminders cover review backlog and stalled work. They are private durable direct notifications, deduplicated by condition episode across restarts, immediate for Agents, and consumed only by reading the Task Thread. The Host uses no timer; an entirely silent Team does not wake itself at a threshold. The first deployment can raise one reminder for each already-eligible historical episode on its next Team event.
23	- Agent `team_thread` renders a discussion's derived Task cards with current status and accountable owner. Human boards name the accountable owner, flag work awaiting the reader's acceptance, and disclose a suspended accountable owner.
24	
25	**Changed**
26	
27	- The Client drops its version 1 paths: the old Project feed, `@all` expansion, and the invitation confirmation flow are gone. The Project page is the Main stream plus the board, and a Thread starts through the owner-only 讨论/任务 control.
28	- Exactly one sidebar row carries `aria-current="page"`: a global face (Inbox, Task board) no longer leaves the marker on the Workspace selector beneath it, and the auto-select no longer pulls the seat back to a Workspace overview while a global face stands.
29	
30	## [0.2.5] - 2026-10-24
31	
32	**Upgrade note**
33	
34	- Channel is now Project. New ledger records use `project:` refs, `projectRef` / `project` / `projectRefs` fields, and `team/project-*` kinds; records written before keep their bytes and still read. Compatibility is one-way: a build older than this release cannot open a ledger this release has written to, because it knows neither the `project:` ref spelling nor the `team/project-*` kinds and rejects the whole table at open. There is no interim release that reads both spellings, so install this release on every profile that shares `$DSH_HOME/storages/` at the same time, and treat downgrading below it as unavailable.
35	- The generation swap records a new operation kind, `team/member-session-recycled`, in the durable ledger. An older build reading a ledger that contains one rejects the whole table at open, so downgrading below this release with a ledger that already recorded a swap leaves the Team unavailable until the release is restored. The domain version stays at 1: an additive kind never changes what a stored record means, which is the only thing the number is allowed to move for.
36	
37	**New**
38	
39	- A Project has owners once the ledger adopts rules version 2, which is still a preview: only `DSH_AGENT_TEAM_PREVIEW_RULES=1` adopts it, and the next release makes it the default. The Human owns every Project without being recorded, and grants or withdraws Agent owners from the Project dialog among Agents that participate in the Workspace and are enabled or suspended. Leaving the Workspace, archival, or removal ends an ownership; suspension does not. Writes are non-optimistic and a Host error stays in the section's alert.
40	
41	**Changed**
42	
43	- Channel is renamed to Project on every surface: the Client (项目 in Chinese), the Remote (`createProject`, `updateProject`, `archiveProject`), tool parameters and output (`projectRef`), change scopes (`kind: 'project'`), and the `start_requires_project` rejection. `channel:` refs still resolve wherever a ref is accepted — a tool argument or a ref cited in a Message body — so Agents and older Messages that cite them keep working. Drafts, sidebar order, and the last open page saved in the browser carry over.
44	- Every Member starts restricted to its preset tools plus `working_directory`; a capability allow-list can only narrow that set. Later plugin tools are removed from request schemas and denied direct or nested execution. Same-name replacements reject requests and execution.
45	- When other official or custom plugins are enabled, Team mode filters their undeclared tools but does not filter their injected prompts. Current public Harness APIs do not provide complete per-Member prompt isolation: required contexts can be restored after assembly. Those prompts remain visible without blocking conversation; full plugin compatibility is not certified.
46	- A Member no longer manages its own context. The four context tools (`context_rollover`, `context_checkpoint`, `context_status`, `context_compact`) are gone, and so is the acceptance advice that used to ride a Thread read. The preset delegates in-place reduction to the Harness's `BasicCompactionEngine` through a thin Team admission adapter; the compaction transaction and summary template stay upstream's. A generation swap is a Host decision: `team-context-management.ts` records `team/member-session-recycled` as the Host actor and activates a fresh Session parented at the one it replaces.
47	- An acceptance that concludes a Member's own work now leaves a boundary behind. The Host appends one `<system-reminder>` telling the Member to move durable conclusions into its `memory.md` index and the notes it names, and at or above 128000 measured tokens it also compacts the generation once the Agent settles. A follower who owns nothing on the Task sees the same accept as unread and is left alone, the reminder never promises a compaction the preset cannot run, and one turn spends at most one boundary however many accepted Tasks it reads.
48	- A Member's proactive input trigger is `floor(min(memberCompaction.tokens, window × 0.8, window − 16384))`, with an absolute default of 256000. A 272K model therefore triggers at 217600 without pre-reserving its maximum output. Pending input is counted; tool-result pruning precedes forced upstream reduction with no proportional retained tail. Summary output has its own 16384 cap. Normal output is limited to remaining window space and the original allowance, with temporary limits recomputed rather than persisted as future intent. An insufficient reduction ends the turn explicitly. A window under 20480 tokens cannot hold both fixed reserves, so the policy declines and that route keeps only the Agent's own limits. Disabling `memberCompaction` restores upstream pressure handling; overflow recovery and ordinary Sessions are unchanged.
49	- The Team settings page configures the in-place compaction threshold under 「上下文」: one capacity field (`256K`, `1M`, or a plain count) that writes `memberCompaction.tokens` through the shared configuration form. A blank field clears the override so the group returns to its 256000 default, and only that child path is written — the sibling `enabled` switch and the rest of the Host row keep the values they had.
50	- A cold Member generation is replaced automatically before a wake reaches it. The Host swaps a generation that has been idle for more than an hour and measures more than 128000 context tokens, whether the wake is a notification, a DM, or an activation at startup or resume; every fact the decision cannot establish answers resume, and a generation still holding unprocessed ordinary input keeps its continuity. Three volatile Host-row fields under `wakeRecycle` set it — `enabled`, `idleMs`, `minContextTokens` — and the Team settings page gives them no form.
51	- A swap no longer strands the input it was racing. A queued ordinary message defers the swap before it starts; past that, the commit runs inside `agent.runMaintenance`, so a message arriving mid-swap waits in the durable inbox instead of reaching the generation being retired, and the retiring generation rejects later steps without spending a model request. Original inbox insertions remain available for replay even after a claim. The commit records `inputFromSeq`, the retired log's offset, when it retires a live generation, and the successor replays only that log's input at and after the boundary, deduplicated by Message id against what it already holds. Nothing is copied through process memory and no handoff envelope returns; a legacy transition without `inputFromSeq` keeps its old started-generation skip.
52	- A swapped-in generation is told nothing about the swap. Its first model-facing context is the ordinary per-step injection — identity, `memory.md`, the Workspace list — plus the message that woke it; the handoff envelope, the generation announcement and the crash-time `Context handoff:` steer are all gone, because a successor that is told it received a handoff performs a handoff instead of reading its memory.
53	- A Member works in the directory the work is in. Its Session, Team participation, Claims, and write permissions stay bound to the Workspace it was created in, but its working directory moves: `working_directory` enters a Workspace the Member has joined and leaves it again, so relative paths, searches, new shells, `run_code`, and that checkout's `AGENTS.md` all resolve where the work actually is. The multi-Workspace guidance now says so instead of telling Members to reach across checkouts by absolute path, which silently skipped the other checkout's instructions.
54	- A Member's tool allow-list no longer removes `working_directory`. The restriction narrows capability; it does not confine a Member to its creation checkout, so the Host unions the tool over the configured list the way it already unions the Team tools.
55	- The bundle declares `engines.dsh` beside its DSH peers. DSH decides a plugin's compatibility from that field alone when it is present, so an install on an uncertified Harness now reports one unmet requirement instead of listing every peer package.
56	- A stale-revision rejection now says how the writer's token related to the Thread instead of carrying a lone `tokenUnrecognized` flag: `staleTokenKind` is `unrecognized` for a token this Thread's revisions skipped over, `unknown` for one older than its first fact, and absent for a plain insertion race. The model-facing refusal is unchanged in words, but a caller that read the boolean must read the new field.
57	- The Inbox and feed rows name Claim owners as `liveClaimOwners` rather than `claimOwners`, so the field matches the rule that produces it: owners of live Claims only, empty once the Task is resolved.
58	- A discussion panel's width is the reader's. Opening one gives it the larger share of the surface (52% of it, clamped to 420–960px) instead of a fixed 360px column, and a seam between the panel and the feed drags that share either way with arrow keys as well as the pointer. Both surfaces read one variable, so the feed gives up exactly what the panel takes, the band above gives up the same width so a long Project description ellipsizes beside the seam rather than running under it, and the seat is remembered per browser and re-clamped to whatever surface it reopens on. The panel is the surface's own child rather than the feed's, so it spans the band and the feed as one column: its head now shares the band's identity row — the same 10px inset and 30px row as the Project title — instead of starting under the tab strip, and its foot composer stands on the feed composer's line. The two rules that used to close those two rows are gone; the band's own rule already ends the row they framed. Below 600px the panel covers the feed in the surface's single column, so the band above keeps its width and its identity row stays whole.
59	- The discussion panel's Messages carry the row actions the Thread page gives them. Hovering a row opens the same card — copy, and a quote that fills the panel's own composer with the Message as the reply's parent — and a row that answers another leads with its quote line, which scrolls to the original inside the panel instead of walking the reader to another page. The panel was the one surface rendering Thread rows without the reading language, so quoting from it was impossible without leaving it. The first row of any scroll box took its card's rise as headroom: the rule that was meant to pay for it named a row as the box's own child, which a run wrapper never is, so the first row's card was clipped by the scroll edge on both surfaces.
60	
61	**Removed**
62	
63	- `clearMemberContext` is gone from the Remote surface, and with it the last way for a Human caller to start a Member from a fresh context. Ledgers that recorded `team/member-session-renewed` or `team/member-session-rolled-over` still replay.
64	- The bundle no longer depends on `@contexera/dsh-context-continuity` or `@contexera/dsh-jev`. The Team's context projection and generation coordinator are its own; `scripts/continuity-dir.mjs`, the engine exports (`./compaction-engine`), the copy steps in `generate-typert.mjs`, and the `DSH_CONTEXT_CONTINUITY_DIR` resolution are gone with them. A profile that still states the old `gate`/`jev` fields in the Host row keeps working — the schema is non-strict, so the unknown keys pass through — but nothing reads them, and a `jev.apiKey` left in a real profile stays in plain text until it is deleted by hand.
65	- The Team settings page drops its `jev` endpoint group: the apiBase/model/key controls, the reachability line, and the 14 locale keys behind them. The page is identity, the compaction threshold, the environment check, and the version footnote.
66	- A Task's Thread band states the Task rather than listing its work queue: the `Claims · N` disclosure is gone with its row layout, its empty line and its three state words. A Claim still reaches a reader as the fact that recorded it — the activity line in the timeline — and as the owners drawn on a feed entry row, and the early-accept dialog still lists the open Claims it will complete, because that list is what the acceptance is decided on. What went is the surface that listed Claims on demand.
67	- `AgentTeamHumanProfileResult.updateAvailable` is gone. `latestVersion` carries the fact on its own: present exactly when a newer release is known, absent while the check has not observed one — or is disabled, offline, or failed. A caller that treated `updateAvailable: false` as "up to date" was reading four different states as one.
68	
69	**Fixed**
70	
71	- A fenced code block in a message body follows the code-size setting again. DSH 0.2.1-rc.2 moved the Markdown code-block size onto `--dsh-code-font-delta` while its leading stayed on that same delta, so the Team Client's own fixed 13px held the words still while the lines around them grew with the setting: at 16px the block rendered 13px words on a 24px line. It now renders 13px at the default setting and moves with the setting on the same px-delta pattern the content axis uses.
72	
73	## [0.2.4] - 2026-10-17
74	
75	**Changed**
76	
77	- The Channel page reads one timeline as either a feed or a board. A the `Channel | Board` tab strip under the header switches between them, speaking the shipped session page's tab language. The board sorts the same projection into four Task-status columns — `To do`, `In progress`, `In review`, `Done` — and reads only the window the feed has already loaded, so opening the tab is not an unbounded read and the feed's own `Load older messages` is how it reaches older work. It is the one Team surface allowed past the 880px reading column, up to 1240px, because four status columns are a scanning surface. Resolved cards dim rather than hide; an empty column states its own `0` in the head instead of drawing a placeholder row.
78	- A taskless discussion opens beside the Channel feed instead of on a page of its own. A taskless Thread's entry row opens a right-hand panel that names the discussion, reads its facts with the usual day separators and runs, answers in the ordinary composer at the same draft key, and offers `Convert to Task` — which, on success, closes the panel as the reader walks into the new Task's Thread page. A read committed in the panel clears its feed row's unread capsule immediately. A Task's entry still walks into the Thread page, where Claims and acceptance live. The panel's 360px seat is reserved only while it is open: an always-on reservation would spend a sixth of a 1440px viewport on an empty band and charge every line of the feed for it. Below 600px the panel covers the stage whole.
79	- The Channel page's header is the shipped session header's shape: one identity row carrying the Channel title with its description beside it on the title's baseline, clamped to one line with the full text on its `title`, and the `Channel | Board` strip on the band's own closing rule. The band is pane chrome rather than a centered column — the shipped session header leaks left to a 20px inset while its transcript stays centered, so the title and the words under it deliberately sit on different x positions, and the Team surfaces copy that arrangement. The band's member and online counts are gone, and so is its back-to-Channels row — the browsing sidebar already lists every Channel and marks the selected one, so a page-level way back was a second control for one destination. The description no longer gets a line of its own, so the band is the same height however much someone wrote into it.
80	- A resolved Task's feed entry row slims to a footnote: `Task #N · <status word> · <MM-DD>`, the day it landed, instead of printing follow-up recency on every finished row. The owner stack and status dot stand down with it — the board owns scanning resolved work — while the unread capsule stays, because a resolved Thread can still be answered and the precise instant stays on the control's `title`.
81	- Team mode's way back to the conversation takes over the shipped New Session bar's slot instead of sitting in the sidebar's footer: it is the first row of the browsing region, directly under the shell's brand row and above the Inbox card, and the narrow rail's first icon. The mode hides that bar, so one bar stands in that position in either mode and only its label changes — the same 38px elevated slab and l3 hairline, reading `Chat` with the glyph pointing back, on the shipped bar's own box: it measures 14px to 266px in the 280px sidebar, the same box the shipped bar occupies, and the browser test measures both in one render and requires them equal — the group's ink is nudged 2.5px back because the chevron's mark sits off-centre inside its box, so a row centred by box alone reads as off-centre. The browsing column beneath it stands on the shipped browser's own content box, so its section headers and rows share the shipped rows' left edge, and it scrolls one way only: the vertical axis, with the bar's space reserved rather than conditional so a growing list never shifts the rows sideways. The brand row itself cannot carry the control — that row is the shipped New Session button on non-macOS and a window-drag surface on macOS, and its mark is `aria-hidden`, so it offers neither a place for a second control nor an accessible name. The members entry and its read-only roster dialog are retired, because the Agent panel already lists every Member with its actions. The footer's settings seat is left to the shipped Settings row, which now keeps it in both modes; the Team's own settings page registers on `settings.section` and stays reachable.
82	- A Message's avatar is 34px instead of 28px, and the author line is levelled with it: the face drops 5px from the name row's top edge so its top meets the author name's capitals, and the name and its time share one baseline — the arrangement Raft gives its own Message row, whose avatars are also level with their author lines. The seat is `--team-identity-seat`, the one place the face's size is stated, so the continuation row's in-seat time and the hairlines that hug the text column follow it with no second edit; it is declared on the shared conversation surface, so the Channel feed — which renders the same rows — follows it too.
83	- Attention and direct messages now have their own tools instead of sharing one with reading and replying. `team_attention` answers only "am I following this Thread" with three parameters no read action needs, and `team_dm` addresses a person with a `memberRef` and a `body` and nothing else. `team_thread` reads and `team_message` writes Threads, so neither carries a branch for the other's job. Sessions recorded before the split still fold correctly: a `follow` logged under `team_thread` is decoded to the same boundary it always was, while no new call can carry that name.
84	- A rejected write now answers with the facts that gated it instead of only a count: `unread_required` renders the unread batch and `stale_revision` renders what changed since your token, both in the same shape a `team_thread read` returns them, and both hand back the current revision to retry with. The retry commits without a second read, so a rejection no longer costs a round-trip of its own.
85	- A write no longer needs a read when the unread work is already in front of the model: a direct mention and a DM arrive carrying the Message body, so when every unread Message is on your surface in full, the write goes through without a `team_thread read` first. Reading still advances the same durable state and stays the only thing that does; the exemption records nothing, and an ordinary notice — which carries a count and not the body — still requires the read.
86	- Every Team rejection now names the next action and the value that action takes — a missing `threadRef` says where to copy one, an unknown Claim ref says which command lists your own, an attachment path says what shape it must have. The words come from one registry instead of each call site writing its own, and a test refuses a route sentence written outside it, so a new rejection cannot reach you with a fault you have no way out of.
87	- Taking part in a Channel now means having taken part in one of its Threads: reading, speaking, claiming, or following. A Member named into a Thread sees the Channel from then on, and a Member who never visits a Channel of its Workspace still does not.
88	- Naming a Member with `@Handle` resolves across the whole Workspace's participants, not only the Channel's enrolled roster, and `@all` expands to the Channel's participants rather than its enrolled roster.
89	- Manual Channel member management is retired: the join and remove entry points are gone from the Remote surface and the Client, and the Channel editor carries no member rows. Old ledgers that still carry explicit membership keep loading and replaying unchanged.
90	- The mention picker ranks every Workspace participant by how directly a pick reaches them — this Thread's followers, then Members taking part in the Channel through another Thread, then the rest. A name outside the conversation being written into also drops a weight, though the row stays pickable because the ledger addresses all of them. Weight is the row's whole distinction: no row states a consequence, and a pick the Host stops to confirm is announced by the composer's status line after the send.
91	
92	**Fixed**
93	
94	- A wide Markdown table scrolls inside the Message column instead of painting over the page beside it. The column lays its children out shrink-to-fit, so a ≥4-column table — which the primitive holds at its natural width so its own wrapper can scroll it — had sized that wrapper to the table itself, and the overflow landed on the page outside the column's right edge. The cap is declared at both levels of the body chain, because a body long enough to fold gains a `data-document` wrapper between the column and the Markdown box, and a `max-width` only resolves against the box that contains it.
95	
96	## [0.2.3] - 2026-10-11
97	
98	**New**
99	
100	- A reply can be linked to the Message it answers: the composer quotes one line of the original, resolved by the Host, and answering a Member delivers to them the way naming them does, while answering your own Message notifies nobody.
101	- A Message that names you says so where its actions are, with a `Mentioned you` badge that lights only for Messages that really name you, and your own handle reads as yours inside a Message body.
102	- The notice that a reply mentions you now says what it answers: the author, the first line of the original, and the full ref you hand back.
103	- Read one Message back whole: `team_thread message` returns the verbatim body by ref, which is how you answer one specific Message without re-reading the Thread.
104	- Members stop queueing behind each other: a long wait on one Member no longer holds up another's pause, removal, or configuration edit.
105	- Member configuration edits report their effect: whether the accepted row was applied now, already in force, or saved for the next activation — and a failed apply leaves a routable diagnostic instead of silently skipping.
106	- A Team wake canceled before the Member can start its turn is now visible instead of silent.
107	
108	**Improved**
109	
110	- Team moves into the sidebar's panel rail beside Plugins, and the plugin list shows Team's own artwork instead of the default placeholder.
111	- Reading the same data on one surface costs one request, a late response never overwrites a fresher result, and a reconnect still fetches what is current.
112	- A read that fails keeps the last number it had and says so, so the Inbox badge and the Channel's unread count no longer drop to empty or zero.
113	- A Message states its own time: rows that already carry an identity line state the instant beside the name, the time stays inside the avatar seat, and reading a Thread on a later day no longer paints a dated label across it.
114	- The Inbox says when the unread queue continues past the rows it shows, instead of letting a full page read as all of it.
115	
116	**Fixed**
117	
118	- Starting a Member from a new context no longer names the caller in the Session id, and a Thread whose history read fails keeps its action for loading older messages — that same action is the retry.
119	- Creating or editing a Member with a model provider the Host has no adapter for is rejected on the spot, naming the provider, instead of producing a Member whose first turn fails.
120	- Opening a Member's Session from its sidebar row now says so when it fails, instead of doing nothing while the row still marks itself as current.
121	- A new Member's private-memory index starts as a bare structural skeleton rather than prose that has to be replaced afterwards.
122	- Quoting your own Message promises nobody a delivery, and a Message's time, mention badge, and quote delivery are stated the way the reader meets them.
123	
124	**Other changes**
125	
126	- The bundled context-continuity engine moves to `0.4.0`, and Team asks the engine's one anchor rule instead of restating it.
127	- `sendMessage` stops creating a Task unless it is asked for one: `asTask: true` is now required to hang a Task off it.
128	- `updateMember` becomes a partial update: a field left out keeps its value, and clearing a `model` or `capabilities` override takes an explicit `null`.
129	
130	**Compatibility**

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project are documented in this file. The format follows [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/) and Semantic Versioning. Team bundle versions evolve independently of DeepSeek Harness versions; DeepSeek Harness compatibility is expressed through `peerDependencies` and [`docs/dsh-release-compatibility.md`](docs/dsh-release-compatibility.md).

## [Unreleased]

**Upgrade note**

- Rules version 2 is now the default and the `DSH_AGENT_TEAM_PREVIEW_RULES` preview switch is gone: this build adopts version 2 on every ledger it opens and no longer writes the version 1 kinds it replaced (`team/message-sent`; they replay inside version 1 segments only). A build at or below 0.2.5 refuses a ledger this build has opened, so install this release on every profile that shares `$DSH_HOME/storages/` before opening the Team anywhere, and back up `agent_team.sqlite` first. A ledger written by the unreleased 06/07 dev builds of this train still opens: their Task starts without a creation activity and their Claim transitions without responsibility markers replay exactly as those builds wrote them.

**New**

- Tasks carry one accountable owner. An Agent Project owner creating a Task becomes accountable by default; the Human may name any owner. Accountability transfers explicitly to another owner or the Human; when an owner is withdrawn, archived, removed, or leaves a Workspace, every open Task it was accountable for returns to the Human in the same operation with a public transfer activity.
- Acceptance is separated from execution: an Agent may accept a Task only once it is `in_review` and only if it never held any Claim on it, released ones included; the Human keeps early acceptance. Close, reopen, and transfer belong to the Human and the current accountable owner.
- Responsibility events reach the Inbox as direct facts regardless of Attention: being made accountable, entering review, a Task left unowned, reopen, and needs-your-acceptance when the accountable owner executed the work.
- A Task may record its originating discussion (`sourceThreadRefs`, immutable, same Project); sourced Tasks leave the Main stream and appear as read-only cards inside the discussions they came from. The board adds the `accountable` relation and flags Tasks awaiting an owner's acceptance.
- `team_task` gains `accept`, `close`, `reopen`, and `transfer`; `team_message.start` accepts an accountable owner and source discussions for Tasks. The persona and the `team-domain-model` skill state the accountable/verifier split.
- Notices are delivered by role. A Project owner's Main stream posts, new discussions, mentions, replies, and ownership events wake immediately; an owner's or Task owner's ordinary Thread updates accumulate per Member per Thread and summarize once at five. The sender's own messages never enter the sender's Inbox.
- Every visible Project carries one Main stream unread row in the Inbox, shared by the Human and Agents; `team_inbox` and the Human's inbox count agree.
- The task board: a `taskBoard` Host projection and Remote method lists every visible Project's open Tasks plus the last five finished per Project, and names the reader its `humanMemberId`. The Web Client reads this projection in both places — the Project board tab and the cross-Workspace Task board page the sidebar's 任务看板 entry opens (its own checklist glyph, a narrow-rail button, cards that say 「你负责」, and an empty state that stands alone without column heads). `team_claim` is merged into `team_task` (`board`, `list`, `claim`, `done`, `release`, `promote`); `team_view` no longer returns active task threads.
- The team-member persona is rewritten for project ownership and ships the `team-domain-model` core skill.
- Event-evaluated Task reminders cover review backlog and stalled work. They are private durable direct notifications, deduplicated by condition episode across restarts, immediate for Agents, and consumed only by reading the Task Thread. The Host uses no timer; an entirely silent Team does not wake itself at a threshold. The first deployment can raise one reminder for each already-eligible historical episode on its next Team event.
- Agent `team_thread` renders a discussion's derived Task cards with current status and accountable owner. Human boards name the accountable owner, flag work awaiting the reader's acceptance, and disclose a suspended accountable owner.

**Changed**

- The Client drops its version 1 paths: the old Project feed, `@all` expansion, and the invitation confirmation flow are gone. The Project page is the Main stream plus the board, and a Thread starts through the owner-only 讨论/任务 control.
- Exactly one sidebar row carries `aria-current="page"`: a global face (Inbox, Task board) no longer leaves the marker on the Workspace selector beneath it, and the auto-select no longer pulls the seat back to a Workspace overview while a global face stands.

## [0.2.5] - 2026-10-24

**Upgrade note**

- Channel is now Project. New ledger records use `project:` refs, `projectRef` / `project` / `projectRefs` fields, and `team/project-*` kinds; records written before keep their bytes and still read. Compatibility is one-way: a build older than this release cannot open a ledger this release has written to, because it knows neither the `project:` ref spelling nor the `team/project-*` kinds and rejects the whole table at open. There is no interim release that reads both spellings, so install this release on every profile that shares `$DSH_HOME/storages/` at the same time, and treat downgrading below it as unavailable.
- The generation swap records a new operation kind, `team/member-session-recycled`, in the durable ledger. An older build reading a ledger that contains one rejects the whole table at open, so downgrading below this release with a ledger that already recorded a swap leaves the Team unavailable until the release is restored. The domain version stays at 1: an additive kind never changes what a stored record means, which is the only thing the number is allowed to move for.

**New**

- A Project has owners once the ledger adopts rules version 2, which is still a preview: only `DSH_AGENT_TEAM_PREVIEW_RULES=1` adopts it, and the next release makes it the default. The Human owns every Project without being recorded, and grants or withdraws Agent owners from the Project dialog among Agents that participate in the Workspace and are enabled or suspended. Leaving the Workspace, archival, or removal ends an ownership; suspension does not. Writes are non-optimistic and a Host error stays in the section's alert.

**Changed**

- Channel is renamed to Project on every surface: the Client (项目 in Chinese), the Remote (`createProject`, `updateProject`, `archiveProject`), tool parameters and output (`projectRef`), change scopes (`kind: 'project'`), and the `start_requires_project` rejection. `channel:` refs still resolve wherever a ref is accepted — a tool argument or a ref cited in a Message body — so Agents and older Messages that cite them keep working. Drafts, sidebar order, and the last open page saved in the browser carry over.
- Every Member starts restricted to its preset tools plus `working_directory`; a capability allow-list can only narrow that set. Later plugin tools are removed from request schemas and denied direct or nested execution. Same-name replacements reject requests and execution.
- When other official or custom plugins are enabled, Team mode filters their undeclared tools but does not filter their injected prompts. Current public Harness APIs do not provide complete per-Member prompt isolation: required contexts can be restored after assembly. Those prompts remain visible without blocking conversation; full plugin compatibility is not certified.
- A Member no longer manages its own context. The four context tools (`context_rollover`, `context_checkpoint`, `context_status`, `context_compact`) are gone, and so is the acceptance advice that used to ride a Thread read. The preset delegates in-place reduction to the Harness's `BasicCompactionEngine` through a thin Team admission adapter; the compaction transaction and summary template stay upstream's. A generation swap is a Host decision: `team-context-management.ts` records `team/member-session-recycled` as the Host actor and activates a fresh Session parented at the one it replaces.
- An acceptance that concludes a Member's own work now leaves a boundary behind. The Host appends one `<system-reminder>` telling the Member to move durable conclusions into its `memory.md` index and the notes it names, and at or above 128000 measured tokens it also compacts the generation once the Agent settles. A follower who owns nothing on the Task sees the same accept as unread and is left alone, the reminder never promises a compaction the preset cannot run, and one turn spends at most one boundary however many accepted Tasks it reads.
- A Member's proactive input trigger is `floor(min(memberCompaction.tokens, window × 0.8, window − 16384))`, with an absolute default of 256000. A 272K model therefore triggers at 217600 without pre-reserving its maximum output. Pending input is counted; tool-result pruning precedes forced upstream reduction with no proportional retained tail. Summary output has its own 16384 cap. Normal output is limited to remaining window space and the original allowance, with temporary limits recomputed rather than persisted as future intent. An insufficient reduction ends the turn explicitly. A window under 20480 tokens cannot hold both fixed reserves, so the policy declines and that route keeps only the Agent's own limits. Disabling `memberCompaction` restores upstream pressure handling; overflow recovery and ordinary Sessions are unchanged.
- The Team settings page configures the in-place compaction threshold under 「上下文」: one capacity field (`256K`, `1M`, or a plain count) that writes `memberCompaction.tokens` through the shared configuration form. A blank field clears the override so the group returns to its 256000 default, and only that child path is written — the sibling `enabled` switch and the rest of the Host row keep the values they had.
- A cold Member generation is replaced automatically before a wake reaches it. The Host swaps a generation that has been idle for more than an hour and measures more than 128000 context tokens, whether the wake is a notification, a DM, or an activation at startup or resume; every fact the decision cannot establish answers resume, and a generation still holding unprocessed ordinary input keeps its continuity. Three volatile Host-row fields under `wakeRecycle` set it — `enabled`, `idleMs`, `minContextTokens` — and the Team settings page gives them no form.
- A swap no longer strands the input it was racing. A queued ordinary message defers the swap before it starts; past that, the commit runs inside `agent.runMaintenance`, so a message arriving mid-swap waits in the durable inbox instead of reaching the generation being retired, and the retiring generation rejects later steps without spending a model request. Original inbox insertions remain available for replay even after a claim. The commit records `inputFromSeq`, the retired log's offset, when it retires a live generation, and the successor replays only that log's input at and after the boundary, deduplicated by Message id against what it already holds. Nothing is copied through process memory and no handoff envelope returns; a legacy transition without `inputFromSeq` keeps its old started-generation skip.
- A swapped-in generation is told nothing about the swap. Its first model-facing context is the ordinary per-step injection — identity, `memory.md`, the Workspace list — plus the message that woke it; the handoff envelope, the generation announcement and the crash-time `Context handoff:` steer are all gone, because a successor that is told it received a handoff performs a handoff instead of reading its memory.
- A Member works in the directory the work is in. Its Session, Team participation, Claims, and write permissions stay bound to the Workspace it was created in, but its working directory moves: `working_directory` enters a Workspace the Member has joined and leaves it again, so relative paths, searches, new shells, `run_code`, and that checkout's `AGENTS.md` all resolve where the work actually is. The multi-Workspace guidance now says so instead of telling Members to reach across checkouts by absolute path, which silently skipped the other checkout's instructions.
- A Member's tool allow-list no longer removes `working_directory`. The restriction narrows capability; it does not confine a Member to its creation checkout, so the Host unions the tool over the configured list the way it already unions the Team tools.
- The bundle declares `engines.dsh` beside its DSH peers. DSH decides a plugin's compatibility from that field alone when it is present, so an install on an uncertified Harness now reports one unmet requirement instead of listing every peer package.
- A stale-revision rejection now says how the writer's token related to the Thread instead of carrying a lone `tokenUnrecognized` flag: `staleTokenKind` is `unrecognized` for a token this Thread's revisions skipped over, `unknown` for one older than its first fact, and absent for a plain insertion race. The model-facing refusal is unchanged in words, but a caller that read the boolean must read the new field.
- The Inbox and feed rows name Claim owners as `liveClaimOwners` rather than `claimOwners`, so the field matches the rule that produces it: owners of live Claims only, empty once the Task is resolved.
- A discussion panel's width is the reader's. Opening one gives it the larger share of the surface (52% of it, clamped to 420–960px) instead of a fixed 360px column, and a seam between the panel and the feed drags that share either way with arrow keys as well as the pointer. Both surfaces read one variable, so the feed gives up exactly what the panel takes, the band above gives up the same width so a long Project description ellipsizes beside the seam rather than running under it, and the seat is remembered per browser and re-clamped to whatever surface it reopens on. The panel is the surface's own child rather than the feed's, so it spans the band and the feed as one column: its head now shares the band's identity row — the same 10px inset and 30px row as the Project title — instead of starting under the tab strip, and its foot composer stands on the feed composer's line. The two rules that used to close those two rows are gone; the band's own rule already ends the row they framed. Below 600px the panel covers the feed in the surface's single column, so the band above keeps its width and its identity row stays whole.
- The discussion panel's Messages carry the row actions the Thread page gives them. Hovering a row opens the same card — copy, and a quote that fills the panel's own composer with the Message as the reply's parent — and a row that answers another leads with its quote line, which scrolls to the original inside the panel instead of walking the reader to another page. The panel was the one surface rendering Thread rows without the reading language, so quoting from it was impossible without leaving it. The first row of any scroll box took its card's rise as headroom: the rule that was meant to pay for it named a row as the box's own child, which a run wrapper never is, so the first row's card was clipped by the scroll edge on both surfaces.

**Removed**

- `clearMemberContext` is gone from the Remote surface, and with it the last way for a Human caller to start a Member from a fresh context. Ledgers that recorded `team/member-session-renewed` or `team/member-session-rolled-over` still replay.
- The bundle no longer depends on `@contexera/dsh-context-continuity` or `@contexera/dsh-jev`. The Team's context projection and generation coordinator are its own; `scripts/continuity-dir.mjs`, the engine exports (`./compaction-engine`), the copy steps in `generate-typert.mjs`, and the `DSH_CONTEXT_CONTINUITY_DIR` resolution are gone with them. A profile that still states the old `gate`/`jev` fields in the Host row keeps working — the schema is non-strict, so the unknown keys pass through — but nothing reads them, and a `jev.apiKey` left in a real profile stays in plain text until it is deleted by hand.
- The Team settings page drops its `jev` endpoint group: the apiBase/model/key controls, the reachability line, and the 14 locale keys behind them. The page is identity, the compaction threshold, the environment check, and the version footnote.
- A Task's Thread band states the Task rather than listing its work queue: the `Claims · N` disclosure is gone with its row layout, its empty line and its three state words. A Claim still reaches a reader as the fact that recorded it — the activity line in the timeline — and as the owners drawn on a feed entry row, and the early-accept dialog still lists the open Claims it will complete, because that list is what the acceptance is decided on. What went is the surface that listed Claims on demand.
- `AgentTeamHumanProfileResult.updateAvailable` is gone. `latestVersion` carries the fact on its own: present exactly when a newer release is known, absent while the check has not observed one — or is disabled, offline, or failed. A caller that treated `updateAvailable: false` as "up to date" was reading four different states as one.

**Fixed**

- A fenced code block in a message body follows the code-size setting again. DSH 0.2.1-rc.2 moved the Markdown code-block size onto `--dsh-code-font-delta` while its leading stayed on that same delta, so the Team Client's own fixed 13px held the words still while the lines around them grew with the setting: at 16px the block rendered 13px words on a 24px line. It now renders 13px at the default setting and moves with the setting on the same px-delta pattern the content axis uses.

## [0.2.4] - 2026-10-17

**Changed**

- The Channel page reads one timeline as either a feed or a board. A the `Channel | Board` tab strip under the header switches between them, speaking the shipped session page's tab language. The board sorts the same projection into four Task-status columns — `To do`, `In progress`, `In review`, `Done` — and reads only the window the feed has already loaded, so opening the tab is not an unbounded read and the feed's own `Load older messages` is how it reaches older work. It is the one Team surface allowed past the 880px reading column, up to 1240px, because four status columns are a scanning surface. Resolved cards dim rather than hide; an empty column states its own `0` in the head instead of drawing a placeholder row.
- A taskless discussion opens beside the Channel feed instead of on a page of its own. A taskless Thread's entry row opens a right-hand panel that names the discussion, reads its facts with the usual day separators and runs, answers in the ordinary composer at the same draft key, and offers `Convert to Task` — which, on success, closes the panel as the reader walks into the new Task's Thread page. A read committed in the panel clears its feed row's unread capsule immediately. A Task's entry still walks into the Thread page, where Claims and acceptance live. The panel's 360px seat is reserved only while it is open: an always-on reservation would spend a sixth of a 1440px viewport on an empty band and charge every line of the feed for it. Below 600px the panel covers the stage whole.
- The Channel page's header is the shipped session header's shape: one identity row carrying the Channel title with its description beside it on the title's baseline, clamped to one line with the full text on its `title`, and the `Channel | Board` strip on the band's own closing rule. The band is pane chrome rather than a centered column — the shipped session header leaks left to a 20px inset while its transcript stays centered, so the title and the words under it deliberately sit on different x positions, and the Team surfaces copy that arrangement. The band's member and online counts are gone, and so is its back-to-Channels row — the browsing sidebar already lists every Channel and marks the selected one, so a page-level way back was a second control for one destination. The description no longer gets a line of its own, so the band is the same height however much someone wrote into it.
- A resolved Task's feed entry row slims to a footnote: `Task #N · <status word> · <MM-DD>`, the day it landed, instead of printing follow-up recency on every finished row. The owner stack and status dot stand down with it — the board owns scanning resolved work — while the unread capsule stays, because a resolved Thread can still be answered and the precise instant stays on the control's `title`.
- Team mode's way back to the conversation takes over the shipped New Session bar's slot instead of sitting in the sidebar's footer: it is the first row of the browsing region, directly under the shell's brand row and above the Inbox card, and the narrow rail's first icon. The mode hides that bar, so one bar stands in that position in either mode and only its label changes — the same 38px elevated slab and l3 hairline, reading `Chat` with the glyph pointing back, on the shipped bar's own box: it measures 14px to 266px in the 280px sidebar, the same box the shipped bar occupies, and the browser test measures both in one render and requires them equal — the group's ink is nudged 2.5px back because the chevron's mark sits off-centre inside its box, so a row centred by box alone reads as off-centre. The browsing column beneath it stands on the shipped browser's own content box, so its section headers and rows share the shipped rows' left edge, and it scrolls one way only: the vertical axis, with the bar's space reserved rather than conditional so a growing list never shifts the rows sideways. The brand row itself cannot carry the control — that row is the shipped New Session button on non-macOS and a window-drag surface on macOS, and its mark is `aria-hidden`, so it offers neither a place for a second control nor an accessible name. The members entry and its read-only roster dialog are retired, because the Agent panel already lists every Member with its actions. The footer's settings seat is left to the shipped Settings row, which now keeps it in both modes; the Team's own settings page registers on `settings.section` and stays reachable.
- A Message's avatar is 34px instead of 28px, and the author line is levelled with it: the face drops 5px from the name row's top edge so its top meets the author name's capitals, and the name and its time share one baseline — the arrangement Raft gives its own Message row, whose avatars are also level with their author lines. The seat is `--team-identity-seat`, the one place the face's size is stated, so the continuation row's in-seat time and the hairlines that hug the text column follow it with no second edit; it is declared on the shared conversation surface, so the Channel feed — which renders the same rows — follows it too.
- Attention and direct messages now have their own tools instead of sharing one with reading and replying. `team_attention` answers only "am I following this Thread" with three parameters no read action needs, and `team_dm` addresses a person with a `memberRef` and a `body` and nothing else. `team_thread` reads and `team_message` writes Threads, so neither carries a branch for the other's job. Sessions recorded before the split still fold correctly: a `follow` logged under `team_thread` is decoded to the same boundary it always was, while no new call can carry that name.
- A rejected write now answers with the facts that gated it instead of only a count: `unread_required` renders the unread batch and `stale_revision` renders what changed since your token, both in the same shape a `team_thread read` returns them, and both hand back the current revision to retry with. The retry commits without a second read, so a rejection no longer costs a round-trip of its own.
- A write no longer needs a read when the unread work is already in front of the model: a direct mention and a DM arrive carrying the Message body, so when every unread Message is on your surface in full, the write goes through without a `team_thread read` first. Reading still advances the same durable state and stays the only thing that does; the exemption records nothing, and an ordinary notice — which carries a count and not the body — still requires the read.
- Every Team rejection now names the next action and the value that action takes — a missing `threadRef` says where to copy one, an unknown Claim ref says which command lists your own, an attachment path says what shape it must have. The words come from one registry instead of each call site writing its own, and a test refuses a route sentence written outside it, so a new rejection cannot reach you with a fault you have no way out of.
- Taking part in a Channel now means having taken part in one of its Threads: reading, speaking, claiming, or following. A Member named into a Thread sees the Channel from then on, and a Member who never visits a Channel of its Workspace still does not.
- Naming a Member with `@Handle` resolves across the whole Workspace's participants, not only the Channel's enrolled roster, and `@all` expands to the Channel's participants rather than its enrolled roster.
- Manual Channel member management is retired: the join and remove entry points are gone from the Remote surface and the Client, and the Channel editor carries no member rows. Old ledgers that still carry explicit membership keep loading and replaying unchanged.
- The mention picker ranks every Workspace participant by how directly a pick reaches them — this Thread's followers, then Members taking part in the Channel through another Thread, then the rest. A name outside the conversation being written into also drops a weight, though the row stays pickable because the ledger addresses all of them. Weight is the row's whole distinction: no row states a consequence, and a pick the Host stops to confirm is announced by the composer's status line after the send.

**Fixed**

- A wide Markdown table scrolls inside the Message column instead of painting over the page beside it. The column lays its children out shrink-to-fit, so a ≥4-column table — which the primitive holds at its natural width so its own wrapper can scroll it — had sized that wrapper to the table itself, and the overflow landed on the page outside the column's right edge. The cap is declared at both levels of the body chain, because a body long enough to fold gains a `data-document` wrapper between the column and the Markdown box, and a `max-width` only resolves against the box that contains it.

## [0.2.3] - 2026-10-11

**New**

- A reply can be linked to the Message it answers: the composer quotes one line of the original, resolved by the Host, and answering a Member delivers to them the way naming them does, while answering your own Message notifies nobody.
- A Message that names you says so where its actions are, with a `Mentioned you` badge that lights only for Messages that really name you, and your own handle reads as yours inside a Message body.
- The notice that a reply mentions you now says what it answers: the author, the first line of the original, and the full ref you hand back.
- Read one Message back whole: `team_thread message` returns the verbatim body by ref, which is how you answer one specific Message without re-reading the Thread.
- Members stop queueing behind each other: a long wait on one Member no longer holds up another's pause, removal, or configuration edit.
- Member configuration edits report their effect: whether the accepted row was applied now, already in force, or saved for the next activation — and a failed apply leaves a routable diagnostic instead of silently skipping.
- A Team wake canceled before the Member can start its turn is now visible instead of silent.

**Improved**

- Team moves into the sidebar's panel rail beside Plugins, and the plugin list shows Team's own artwork instead of the default placeholder.
- Reading the same data on one surface costs one request, a late response never overwrites a fresher result, and a reconnect still fetches what is current.
- A read that fails keeps the last number it had and says so, so the Inbox badge and the Channel's unread count no longer drop to empty or zero.
- A Message states its own time: rows that already carry an identity line state the instant beside the name, the time stays inside the avatar seat, and reading a Thread on a later day no longer paints a dated label across it.
- The Inbox says when the unread queue continues past the rows it shows, instead of letting a full page read as all of it.

**Fixed**

- Starting a Member from a new context no longer names the caller in the Session id, and a Thread whose history read fails keeps its action for loading older messages — that same action is the retry.
- Creating or editing a Member with a model provider the Host has no adapter for is rejected on the spot, naming the provider, instead of producing a Member whose first turn fails.
- Opening a Member's Session from its sidebar row now says so when it fails, instead of doing nothing while the row still marks itself as current.
- A new Member's private-memory index starts as a bare structural skeleton rather than prose that has to be replaced afterwards.
- Quoting your own Message promises nobody a delivery, and a Message's time, mention badge, and quote delivery are stated the way the reader meets them.

**Other changes**

- The bundled context-continuity engine moves to `0.4.0`, and Team asks the engine's one anchor rule instead of restating it.
- `sendMessage` stops creating a Task unless it is asked for one: `asTask: true` is now required to hang a Task off it.
- `updateMember` becomes a partial update: a field left out keeps its value, and clearing a `model` or `capabilities` override takes an explicit `null`.

**Compatibility**
